issues.description: Frozen metadata and exact bounded reads identify accessible Worldscope annual, U.S./international I/B/E/S summary, and WRDS ESG panel/crosswalk candidates. They do not show equivalence to the six regional Worldscope/I/B/E/S exports or fifteen ASSET4 slices: `recno` is not proven to equal `NUMEST`, TRESG uses OrgId/FisYear and Isin rather than the authored wc06008/wc05350 pair, and complete product/period/field population remains unverified.

The two directly consumed author-prepared workbooks are absent. Appendix H provides a compatibility-limited 2014 collection alternative, but it does not establish both workbook roles, the second workbook's raw-column rename/hand-review field, the complete population or the wc06008/year key and Master1 merge contracts. X login/indexing and Wayback capture limits are documented; no issuer-specific record was checked.

The source sets PATH to an author-specific absolute Windows directory. A coherent relative project root and Temp/Output staging are needed for a working-copy run, with every source and output path kept under the same root.

Stata 18 is available; version/which metadata found the actively invoked winsor, ffind, eststo and esttab commands, but did not find psmatch2, pstest or rbounds. These are free setup dependencies named by the source's install header; no installation or author-code trial occurred.

Three `use` calls pass `replace`; the official Stata 18 `use` syntax lists `clear` and `nolabel`. A working-copy change to `clear` is supported and preserves the intended load-over-current-data operation.

evidence.description: Appendix H describes 2014 annual reports, company web pages archived through Wayback Machine, and Twitter as manual source channels.
evidence.quote:
(1) We examine CSR information (if any information is available) in annual reports 2014. Keywords
        for search in pdf files: CSR, sustainability, environment, social, responsibility, ESG, etc. In
        addition, we check the company webpage for separate documents or other CSR-related
        information with the Wayback Machine between the last quarter of 2014 and the first quarter of
        2015. Finally, we analyze whether firms announce CSR activities via Twitter during the year
        2014. If there is no information about CSR at all, the firm is classified as 0.

evidence.description: For U.S. high-exposure firms Appendix H names 2014 EDGAR Forms 8-K, 10-K, 20-F, and 40-F and web/Twitter sources.
evidence.quote:
(2) For the U.S. high-exposure firms, we examine CSR information from all Forms 8-K, 10-K, 20-
        F, and 40-F filed on EDGAR in calendar year 2014 (following SASB, see survey by Christensen
        et al. [2019, p.45]). In addition, we also use company webpage information with the Wayback
        Machine as well as Twitter information as potential sources to identify new CSR initiatives.

evidence.description: Appendix H describes the 2014 initiative coding and distinguishes new initiatives, committees, data systems, SOC, and ENV.
evidence.quote:
(5) We identify firms that have initiated at least one CSR project in 2014 (classification = 1). Text
        that has triggered a classification of 1 (list is not exhaustive).

        Keywords: combination of (a) and (b)

          (a) In 2014, during 2014, during the year, in the current period…

          (b) Launched, initiated, new program, joined, designed, implemented, created, established,
              introduced… Highlighted in YELLOW is the text that triggers the classification equal to
              1.

        However, the words “continued”, “further improved, “awarded for”, “donated”, “expended” are
        not sufficient to trigger classification equal to 1 because it does not imply a new initiative; we
        highlighted this in GREEN.

    (6) For firms with new initiatives, we distinguish between initiative into new CSR committees, new
        CSR data management systems, and other (real) initiatives. Finally, we split the other (real)
        initiatives into SOC and ENV.

evidence.description: The supplied balanced EU/US sample branch invokes psmatch2, rbounds, and pstest.
evidence.quote:

		psmatch2 TREATMENT`i' $MATCHINGVAR if (TREATMENT`i'|CG`i') & ($PREYEAR) & $EXCLUDE, outcome(OUTCOMEVAR) $CALIPER n($NUMBERNB)
		sum _nn // number of matched neighbors
		
		*(5)Rosenbaum (2002) hidden bias analysis
		gen diff =  OUTCOMEVAR - _OUTCOMEVAR
